title: Kohli and Bumrah Return as India Name Squad for England ODIs. Jaiswal Pays the Price.
excerpt: Shubman Gill will captain a 15-member squad preparing for the 2027 World Cup. Hardik Pandya is ruled out injured. And the man who scored a century in Kohli's absence has been dropped.
body:
Virat Kohli is back. And with him, Jasprit Bumrah.

The Board of Control for Cricket in India on Sunday announced a 15-member ODI squad for the three-match series against England beginning on July 14. Shubman Gill, who led India to a 3-0 sweep of Afghanistan in his first assignment as ODI captain, has been named to lead the side. Shreyas Iyer will serve as vice-captain.

The headline, though, belongs to the names returning — and the one left out.

## The Comeback Trail


![Virat Kohli — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/9b/Virat_Kohli_in_PMO_New_Delhi.jpg)


Kohli, 37, has been out since the IPL 2026 final, where he scored an unbeaten 75 to help Royal Challengers Bengaluru clinch their second title before pulling up with a hamstring injury. He has since been rehabilitating at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, and his inclusion in the squad remains subject to a final fitness clearance.

Bumrah's return is more straightforward. India's premier fast bowler was rested for the Afghanistan ODIs as part of ongoing workload management. In English conditions — overcast skies, sideways movement, a Duke ball that does things no other cricket ball does — his presence is not just welcome but essential. Bumrah will spearhead a pace attack that also includes Arshdeep Singh, Prasidh Krishna, Harshit Rana, and the uncapped Gurnoor Brar, who impressed during the Afghanistan series.

The spin department features Kuldeep Yadav, Axar Patel, and Washington Sundar. Nitish Kumar Reddy adds balance as a pace-bowling allrounder.

## The Man Who Loses His Spot


![Jasprit Bumrah — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/02/Jasprit_Bumrah_in_PMO_New_Delhi.jpg)


The most contentious selection call is the omission of Yashasvi Jaiswal. The left-hander stepped into the squad during Kohli's absence and responded with a century in the final ODI against Afghanistan — exactly the kind of knock that is supposed to make selectors' jobs harder.

It did not, apparently, make the job hard enough. With Kohli's return, Jaiswal has been squeezed out of the 15, a reminder that Indian cricket remains a place where runs alone do not guarantee a seat at the table. Senior players Rohit Sharma and KL Rahul both retain their places.

## Hardik's Body Betrays Him Again

Hardik Pandya is the other significant absentee. The allrounder, who had been recovering from a back spasm, suffered a fresh quadricep injury during rehabilitation. According to reports, the setback will keep him out for longer than the three weeks initially anticipated, ruling him out of the entire England tour — both the five T20Is under Iyer's captaincy starting July 1 and the ODIs that follow.


![Shreyas Iyer — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/ae/Shreyas_Iyer_snapped_at_the_airport_%28Cropped%29.jpg)


India's inability to find a like-for-like replacement for Pandya when he breaks down — and he has broken down with increasing regularity — continues to be one of the team's most persistent structural problems.

## Why England Matters

This is not just another bilateral series. With the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa, Namibia, and Zimbabwe now less than a year away, every ODI India plays is an audition. Gill's leadership will be scrutinised. Kohli's form — or lack of it — will be dissected. And the bowling attack that has to function in conditions tailor-made for swing will determine whether India can win overseas when it counts.

The three ODIs will be played at Edgbaston (July 14), Sophia Gardens in Cardiff (July 17), and Lord's (July 20). Before that, Iyer leads the T20I squad — which includes 15-year-old prodigy Vaibhav Sooryavanshi — into a five-match series starting at Chester-le-Street on July 1.

## The Diaspora Connection

For the roughly 1.8 million people of Indian origin living in the United Kingdom, this tour is the summer's marquee event. India's matches at Edgbaston, Cardiff, and Lord's routinely draw diaspora crowds that transform English grounds into extensions of Indian stadiums — tricolour flags, dhol drums, and a noise level that English cricket has never quite figured out how to match.

Kohli, in particular, is box office in England. His centuries at Edgbaston and Trent Bridge during the 2018 tour remain defining moments for a generation of British Indian cricket fans. Whether or not the 37-year-old has one more transcendent overseas series left in him may well define how this squad — and this World Cup cycle — is remembered.

**India's ODI squad for England:** Shubman Gill (captain), Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli (subject to fitness), Shreyas Iyer (vice-captain), KL Rahul, Ishan Kishan, Washington Sundar, Axar Patel, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Kuldeep Yadav, Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna, Harshit Rana, Arshdeep Singh, Gurnoor Brar.
